name: vscroll-delivery
description: a vertical gesture reaches the app at all. Opens Settings, whose General pane scrolls natively, and pulls on it - if the pane moves, the vertical axis is being delivered. This exists because cgevent could only ever send horizontal scrolls: wheel1 was hard-coded to 0, so no vertical behaviour anywhere was reachable from a scenario. The first attempt at the fix declared TWO axes with the horizontal at zero, and those events posted without any error and moved nothing at all - not this pane, not the sidebar. A vertical-only gesture is wheelCount 1. That failure mode is why this scenario asserts a natively scrollable surface rather than an Atrium-specific one: it separates 'the event arrived' from 'the thing under it responded', and those were confused for an hour.

actions.note: let the browser window finish first paint
Atrium MUST be frontmost or cmd+comma opens Finder Settings instead - observed
open Settings; its menu item is not reachable from a scenario
Over the Settings General pane's body, which scrolls natively. Coordinates read off settings-tab-row's captured frames - the window spans roughly x 0-640, y 250-700.

assertions.desc: The pane's rows must move. A delta of 0 means the vertical event never arrived, which is a harness fault rather than anything about Atrium. Region read off settings-tab-row's captured frames.
